text:
jamie: putting up the node quickstart in our repo and GH Actions job keeps failing with 403 on the generate call. works locally for me.

nora: are you using a service key or personal key in the GH Secrets? GH masks secrets but sometimes people accidentally paste the workspace id into the secret.

jamie: secret is REDWOOD_API_KEY set in org secrets. action logs show: `POST /v1/generate -> 403` and body: `{"error":"billing_required","message":"workspace needs billing configured"}`

carlos: that means the key is workspace-scoped (service key) and the target workspace has no payment method. local dev keys sometimes get temporary credits which is why it worked on your machine.

jamie: hmm, i did create a key from my user profile then uploaded it to GH. i thought that would be fine. can user keys be used in CI?

onboard-bot: :robot_face: Note: user-scoped (personal) API keys can be used in CI but are subject to rate limits and may be revoked if tied to a personal account. Service keys require workspace billing for non-interactive runs. See https://console.redwood.ai/docs/keys.

nora: also check if the action runner is setting a workspace header or env var. We had a case where the sample app dockerfile overwrote REDWOOD_WORKSPACE env to a default sandbox workspace which was not billed.

jamie: good point. our docker-entrypoint.sh exports REDWOOD_WORKSPACE=workspace-sandbox by default. i forgot to strip that for CI.

carlos: quick fix options: 1) remove the hardcoded REDWOOD_WORKSPACE in docker image and let the key determine workspace, 2) set REDWOOD_WORKSPACE in GH Secrets to the billed workspace id, or 3) attach a billing method to the sandbox workspace.

jamie: removed the default env from the image and re-ran actions -> still 403. debug step shows request now includes header `X-Redwood-Workspace: workspace-sandbox` coming from app config.

nora: maybe the app reads a config file baked into the image. grep for X-Redwood-Workspace in repo.

jamie: found it in ./config/defaults.json. it was added in the sample to make local testing easier. changing to null and re-building the image fixed it. GH Actions job is green now. :tada:

devex-bot: Pro tip: add a CI health-check step that calls `/v1/account` and verifies `billing.enabled` before running heavy jobs. Example: `curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/account | jq '.billing.enabled'`

carlos: filing DX follow-up: update quickstart Dockerfile to avoid baking workspace defaults, add `ci-check` workflow template, and small troubleshooting note about 403 vs 401 in README.

jamie: thanks everyone — notes added to our onboarding doc and the sample repo README. will open a PR for the CI workflow template.

nora: extra: consider adding a short `scripts/ci-key-check.sh` that fails fast with a clear message when billing is missing. saves flapping builds.

jamie: yeah i'll add that.
